chapman_chester.text: Chapbooks, hot off the Rows. Roman ones are extra. They are not Roman. I just say that.

then.text: I am busy. I am always busy. It is a point of professional pride.
You'll find I am rarely in the same place twice. That is because I am scheduled to be elsewhere.

else.text: Good afternoon. You are standing on a Roman wall. Fine. You are standing on a Licensed Heritage Asset, pending paperwork.
Gareth Pryce, Regional Director for Wales. And for the border, as of Tuesday. It was a very productive Tuesday.
Dinas Emrys. A small hill, a large pool, and an unlicensed dragon. Disgraceful. No signage, no tickets, no gift shop.
I am going to license it. Politely. I am always polite, you'll find.
I see from your face that you disapprove. I have a form for that. It's a two-page form. It's mostly about your feelings.
Do carry on with your little collection. I'll be in Wales. I'll see you at the gates. Item four on my agenda.

rail_guard.text: Chester. Trains to Wales, the north and anywhere with a nice view.

then.text: Rain on the walls. Good news: the Rows are covered, so the tour moves indoors, sort of.
Lovely day for the walls! Two miles of views, and the pigeons are in a good mood.
Can't see the cathedral in this fog. Trust me, it's there. It's been there ages.

wall_guide.text: These are the best-preserved city walls in Britain, two miles round, and you can walk the whole circuit. I recommend it. The pigeons recommend you don't.
The Romans called this place Deva, after the river. The river is the Dee. It's the same name. They were very efficient and not very imaginative.

then.text: That man in the tweed was measuring the walls with a laser. For 'access reasons'. I hope he's not planning to put a till on the Eastgate clock.
Romans in the rain. My sandals are full of water. Very authentic, very cold.
My cloak's trying to fly back to Rome. Hold on, Marcus. I mean Brian. Either.
The legion's off duty. Brian has to get the bus home and he can't do it in armour.

legionary.text: Ave! I am Marcus. Well, Brian. But Marcus on weekdays.
Chester was Deva Victrix, home of the Twentieth Legion. We built the amphitheatre. It's the biggest in Britain. You're welcome.

chester_verger.text: The cathedral was an abbey for Benedictine monks. Red sandstone, like the walls.
Look up at the ceiling. The monks knew how to pick a ceiling.

then.text: Sun on the Roodee! Perfect day to lose a bit of money in style.
Rain on the course. The horses don't mind. I mind. My shoes mind.

racegoer.text: {greeting} The Roodee has hosted races since 1539. England's oldest racecourse still in use.
I've lost money here for twenty years. It's the finest losing experience in England.

then.text: After rain like this the Dee rises quick. She's in a mood, the goddess river.
Sunshine on the Dee! Everyone wants a boat. I've only got the one.

boatman.text: {greeting} The River Dee. The Romans used it as a port. Legionaries marched up from the quay.
It's a Celtic name, Dyfrdwy, 'goddess river'. She's not always friendly after a downpour.

chester_student.text: Eastgate Clock. 1899. Everyone photographs it. I've seen exactly one person look at the time.
The Rows are two storeys of shops. Nobody agrees why. Chester just likes to be awkward.

chester_lamplighter.text: Evening! Walking the walls with my pole. Chester looks its best by lamplight, like an old painting.
The Eastgate Clock glows at night. Everyone photographs it then too. Still nobody checks the time.
Watch your step on the walls after dark. The Romans didn't build railings, and neither did anyone else.
